lines.japanese: 更衣室で着替えを終えて、労働準備も完了したものの、なにかお腹に違和感。
lines.english: I had changed in the locker room and was ready for work, yet something about my stomach felt wrong.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか、ベルトの穴をひとつ絞って締めちゃいましたかね。よし、ちょっと緩めて、よ、ほっ……あん、腸の中身が下っていく感覚が……あふん。
lines.english: Ah, of course. I’d buckled my belt one hole tighter, hadn’t I? All right, loosen it a little, and... there. Ahhn, I could feel the contents of my bowels descending... Ahhhn.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん、ちょっと事務所から運んでいただきたいものが──」
lines.english: “Chitose, there’s something I’d like you to carry from the office—”

lines.japanese: 「ああハイなんでしょう日和子さん」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, Hiyoko? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「──どうして私が来たとたんズボンを脱ぎはじめるんですか」
lines.english: “—why did you start taking your pants off the instant I arrived?”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　アッ、いや違っ……！」
lines.english: “Huh? Ah! No, you’ve got it—!”

lines.japanese: 今日も今日とて偶然のいたずらに翻弄される俺であった。
lines.english: Once again, fate had played one of its little tricks on me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、これはですね、作業を円滑に進めるためのお色直しでですね！　ええと、そそ、それでなんでしたっけ運び屋の仕事でしたっけ」
lines.english: “Um, you see, this is a costume change designed to ensure the smooth performance of my duties! So, ah... what was it again? You needed something moved?”

lines.japanese: 俺は腰と顔の弛みを引きしめながら、教官のもとへだぼだぼと駆けよりました。
lines.english: Tightening my waistband and my expression alike, I hitched up my baggy pants and hurried over to Coach Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: そのとき店内に、どこか聞き覚えのあるしっとりした低音が……あれ？　なんだこれ？
lines.english: Just then, a strangely familiar, velvety baritone spread through the restaurant... Wait. What was this?

lines.japanese: 「アレキサンダーにご来店中の皆様こんばんは。本日より始まるレイディオＫＫ、ナビゲートさせていただくのはワタクシ『俺のリミッターは法律ごときじゃ縛れない』軽部狩男ことＭＣＫＫです」
lines.english: “Good evening to all our guests here at Alexander. Radio KK begins broadcasting today, and your guide will be yours truly: Karuo ‘No Law Can Hold Back My Limiter’ Karube, otherwise known as MCKK.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……本当に始めたんだ、店内放送……」
lines.english: “Oh... He really went ahead with the in-house radio show...”

lines.japanese: 事務室の一角をブースに見立てて、うっとりオンエア中の３５歳が目に浮かぶようです。
lines.english: I could picture the thirty-five-year-old in raptures, treating a corner of the office as his very own booth.

lines.japanese: たしかに台本書かされたけどさ……冗談であることを願ってたんだよな……。
lines.english: Sure, he’d made me write a script... but I’d been hoping this was all a joke...

lines.japanese: 「さて１２月４日、月曜日の黄昏どきを皆様いかがお過ごしでしょうか。街で見かけるオコジョや雷鳥もすっかり換毛してホワイトウィンターまっさかり、ほとばしる尿も思わずホットな溜息をついていますね」
lines.english: “Now then, how is this Monday twilight, December fourth, treating you? The stoats and ptarmigans about town have shed into their winter coats, white winter is in full swing, and even a steaming jet of urine cannot help but sigh warmly.”

lines.japanese: 「さて尿といえば、進んだ恋人たちのあいだでは、かけたりかけられたり濃厚なラブを確認するためのマストピースとしてすっかりお馴染みになってきました」
lines.english: “And speaking of urine, sophisticated lovers have grown quite accustomed to giving and receiving it as that indispensable finishing touch by which they affirm the depth of their love.”

lines.japanese: 「ただいま当店では、そんなスウィートなパフュームを食卓にドロップすべく、匂いたつような金色のシードルを、フラスコ・尿瓶・目盛り付き紙コップなどで提供させていただくゴールデンキャンペーンを実施中です」
lines.english: “Here at Alexander, we are currently running a Golden Campaign: that we might drop such sweet perfume upon your table, we will serve you a fragrant golden cider in a flask, urinal bottle, graduated paper cup, or vessel of your choice.”

lines.japanese: うわー、無駄に渋い声でなに言ってんだこのおっさんー。
lines.english: Oh, come on. What was this old man saying in that needlessly suave voice?

lines.japanese: ていうか俺の台本、意味ないじゃん。最初の一行ぐらいしか生きてないじゃん。時節柄カップル向けの話をしろとは言ったけど！
lines.english: And what was the point of my script? He’d kept maybe the first line. I’d told him to talk about couples, given the season, but still!

lines.japanese: 幸いなのは、声自体が店のおしゃれな内装に溶けこんでいるため、トークの内容にさえ耳を傾けなければフツーに環境音としてマッチしていることです。おかげでお客様から苦情があがることもなく。
lines.english: Luckily, his voice blended beautifully with the restaurant’s stylish decor. As long as nobody listened to a word he said, it worked perfectly as ambience. Apparently, that was why no one complained.

lines.japanese: 「それではオープニングの一曲目、フリッキー５で『ほほえみジェノサイド』」
lines.english: “And now, our opening number: Fricky Five with ‘Smiling Genocide.’”

lines.japanese: ま、どーでもいいです。どうせ５分ででっち上げたテキトー原稿だったし。ほほジェノさえかけてくれるなら、あとはまあ、どう改変してくれようと──
lines.english: Well, whatever. I’d slapped together that half-assed script in five minutes. As long as he played “Smiling Genocide,” he could mangle the rest however he—

lines.japanese: 「――のはずでしたが、予定を変更してブルマニアデビルのＮＥＷナンバー『食い込みからの離脱～差し込まれた人差し指』をお送りします」
lines.english: “—or so we had planned. Instead, here is Bloomer-Mania Devil’s new number, ‘Breaking Free of the Wedgie ~ The Index Finger Slips Inside.’”

lines.japanese: 「そこまで変えちゃうのかよ！」
lines.english: “You’re changing that too!?”

lines.japanese: 俺はパーソナリティの暴挙に、思わず丸めたおしぼりをスピーカーに投げつけていました。
lines.english: Outraged by the host’s latest offense, I found myself hurling a rolled hand towel at the speaker.

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと日和子さん！　いんすかコレ、この品のない店内放送！」
lines.english: “W-wait, Hiyoko! You’re okay with this!? This vulgar in-store broadcast!?”

lines.japanese: そして自分が構成作家であるにも関わらず、番組自体の違法性を訴える変わり身の速さ。
lines.english: A dazzlingly swift change of sides from the show’s own writer, now denouncing the entire program as a crime.

lines.japanese: 「え、なんすかコレ！　どーなんすか日和子さん！　こんな職権濫用許していいんすか！」
lines.english: “What even is this!? What do you make of it, Hiyoko? Can we allow this shameless abuse of authority!?”

lines.japanese: 「事務室のロッカーの上に段ボールがありますので千歳さんはそれを厨房まで運んでください」
lines.english: “There is a cardboard box on top of the lockers in the office. Please carry it to the kitchen.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、ガン無視だ！」
lines.english: “Whoa. Completely ignored!”

lines.japanese: さすがは日和子さん、マスターの相手をしたら負けだと分かっておられる御様子。すらすらと仕事上の会話を続けておいでです。
lines.english: As expected of Hiyoko: she knew that engaging the boss meant losing. Without missing a beat, she continued our strictly professional conversation.

lines.japanese: 「いやでも、必要以上に無表情なところがまた、如実に怒りを表してますよね」
lines.english: “Though that excessively blank look on your face is making your fury pretty obvious.”

lines.japanese: 「厨房スタッフに必要となるものを確認いただいて、その場で箱の中から渡してしまってください」
lines.english: “Ask the kitchen staff which supplies they require, then give those items to them from the box.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、聞こえてましたよね？　ていうか、いまも続いてるこの壊れかけのレイディオ聞こえてますよね？」
lines.english: “You heard that, right? I mean, this radio on its last legs is still going—you can hear it, can’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「それが済んだら段ボールは必ずもとの場所へ戻すようにしてください。いい加減に済ますとあとの人が迷惑します」
lines.english: “When you finish, be sure to return the box to its original place. If you cut corners, you’ll only cause trouble for the next person.”

lines.japanese: すごうい。まるで、何も聞こえちゃいないんだと自己暗示をかけてるかのようだあ。
lines.english: Amaaaazing. It was as though she were hypnotizing herself: I can’t hear a thing, I can’t hear a thing.

lines.japanese: 「千歳千歳っ、いまの放送聞いた！？」
lines.english: “Chitose, Chitose! Did you hear that broadcast!?”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんの現実逃避を眺めていたら、滑るような小走りで英里子さんがやってきました。お客さんの前では走らないあたり接客業の鑑です。
lines.english: As I watched Hiyoko flee reality, Eriko came gliding over at a quick little trot. She never quite ran in front of the customers—the very model of service-industry professionalism.

lines.japanese: 「聞きましたよ、そりゃ店内にいたら嫌でも聞こえますって。ていうか台本書いたの俺だし」
lines.english: “Of course I heard it. You couldn’t stand inside the restaurant and not hear it. More to the point, I wrote the script.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……黒幕は千歳さんですか……」
lines.english: “I see... So you were the mastermind, Chitose...”

lines.japanese: 「アッ！　いや違っ、あの、業務命令で拒否権なかったんすよ！？　だいたい俺の書いた筋書きは、お子様の情操教育にも適したファミリー向けの内容ですからね？　それをあの不精ヒゲが勝手に──」
lines.english: “Ah! No, wait, that’s not—! It was an order! I had no right to refuse! Besides, my script was wholesome family entertainment fit for impressionable children. Then that stubbly layabout took it and—”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さあ、お前が構成っつーなら尚更だよ。あんな勝手、許していいわけ？」
lines.english: “Chitose, if you’re supposed to be the writer, that’s even worse. You really gonna let him pull whatever he wants?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに許した覚えはないんすけど……」
lines.english: “Well, I don’t recall ever giving my permission...”

lines.japanese: 「英里子さん、もし店長に直訴するなら私も手伝いますけど」
lines.english: “Eriko, if you’re going to take this straight to the Manager, I’d be glad to help.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、マジ？　そしたら意見書みたいの作ってもらおうかな」
lines.english: “Oh, seriously? Then maybe you can draft me a formal petition or something.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、作家さんの作る文書ならさぞかし説得力ありそっすね。これは心強いっす」
lines.english: “Oh, a document by a real writer has gotta be convincing. That’s reassuring.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、じゃあ今から私が改正案だすから、たまひよ筆記よろしく」
lines.english: “All right. I’ll give you my reform proposals, and Tama-chick, you take dictation.”

lines.japanese: 「はい。喜んで協力させていただきます。どうぞ」
lines.english: “Certainly. I will be delighted to cooperate. Please begin.”

lines.japanese: かちかち、とシャーペンをノックして、クリップボードに向かう日和子さん。彼女が業務の手を止めるぐらいだから、よっぽど耐えがたかったんだろうなあ。
lines.english: Hiyoko clicked her mechanical pencil twice and poised it over her clipboard. If this was enough to make her stop working, she must have found the broadcast truly unbearable.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、まずパーソナリティは日野英里子に交替」
lines.english: “First, the host will be replaced by Eriko Hino.”

lines.japanese: 「参加するんだ！」
lines.english: “You’re joining it!?”

lines.japanese: 「だって店長、向いてないでしょ。ベシャリは上手いけど、最近の流行りとか分かってないし」
lines.english: “The Manager’s obviously wrong for the job. Sure, he’s got the gift of gab, but he doesn’t know what’s current.”

lines.japanese: 「論点ずれまくり！」
lines.english: “You’ve missed the point by a mile!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。千歳アシスタントやってもいいよ。私が面白いこと言ったら盛大に笑い声あげる役」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Chitose, you can be my assistant. Whenever I say something funny, your job is to laugh your head off.”

lines.japanese: 「やんねえよ」
lines.english: “Like hell I will.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さん方面からシャーペンの芯的なものがボキリと折れる音がして、思わず俺は男らしい声で拒否していました。
lines.english: I heard something very much like mechanical pencil lead snapping in Hiyoko’s direction, and promptly declined in my manliest voice.

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、私と紀奈子さんの、ほらアレックス２って企画あったじゃん。アレどうなったんだよ。やっつけ番組の構成作家なんていいから、はやく敏腕プロデューサーの仕事しろよコラ、ああん？」
lines.english: “Anyway, remember that Alex Two project with me and Kinako? What happened to that? Quit writing throwaway radio shows and get back to work as our hotshot producer, asshole. Well?”

lines.japanese: 「痛い痛い！　やめて！　シルバートレイの顔面プレスは、実際の痛みより見た目が不様だからなるべくやめて！」
lines.english: “Ow, ow! Stop! Try not to mash a silver tray into my face—it looks even more pathetic than it hurts!”

lines.japanese: 「あああああこの店はどこもかしこもっ！」
lines.english: “Aaaagh! This entire restaurant is out of control!”

lines.japanese: 「痛い痛い痛い！　ツープラトンでのサンドイッチプレスは、両者の力加減が絶妙に噛みあってないと意外に痛いから良い子が真似するとわりかし危険！」
lines.english: “Ow ow ow! A two-person sandwich press hurts more than you’d think unless both people match their pressure just right, so it’s pretty dangerous for good children to imitate!”

lines.japanese: ていうかもうただの八つ当たりじゃん！
lines.english: At this point, they were just taking it out on me!

lines.japanese: ああ、鬼の玉泉教官が、なんだかちょっぴりアレキサンダーの空気に染まってきた気がする。
lines.english: Ah. My demonic Coach Tamaizumi seemed to be absorbing the atmosphere of Alexander, ever so slightly.

lines.japanese: そのときスピーカーからは、次のコーナー『ぎりぎり合法！　僕の私の性犯罪ちっく体験！』の始まる旨が流れていました。
lines.english: Meanwhile, the speakers announced the next segment: “Just Barely Legal! Your Almost-Criminal Sexual Experiences!”

lines.japanese: 「おお鷲介。お前が書いてくれた台本のおかげで、一回目の放送にしてはいい出来になった。感謝するぞ」
lines.english: “Ah, Shusuke. Thanks to your script, the very first broadcast came out rather well. You have my gratitude.”

lines.japanese: 「しないでください。出来はともかく、俺が書いたホンとはほとんど別モノだったんで」
lines.english: “Please don’t. Never mind how it turned out; it bore almost no resemblance to the script I wrote.”

lines.japanese: 休憩時間。スタッフルームのドアを開けると、清々しさ満点のマスターが俺を出迎えました。
lines.english: Break time. I opened the staff-room door to find the boss waiting for me, the very picture of radiant satisfaction.

lines.japanese: 「ははは、なにを照れてるんだこいつう。他の従業員にも胸を張って誇るがいい」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! Look at you, getting all bashful. Hold your head high and boast about it to the other employees.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、他の従業員に肩身が狭くなるんで。くれぐれもマスターひとりの功績ということで」
lines.english: “No, then I’d never be able to look the other employees in the eye. Please be sure to take all the credit yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、そうか？　そんなに俺のトークや進行は素晴らしかったか？」
lines.english: “Heh heh. Is that so? You thought my patter and presentation were that magnificent?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まあ、それは……」
lines.english: “Ah... well, that part...”

lines.japanese: 俺は苦笑しながら頷きました。
lines.english: I nodded with a strained smile.

lines.japanese: ネタの酷ささえ除けば、たしかにマスターのパーソナリティっぷりは、なかなか堂に入っていたと言えましょう。
lines.english: Appalling material aside, the boss had certainly sounded like an old hand behind the microphone.

lines.japanese: 「初めてとは思えないっていうか、こなれてる感があったっすね。パチンコ屋の実況とか、結婚式の司会とか、実はそういう経験あったとか？」
lines.english: “It didn’t sound like your first time. You seemed pretty polished. Have you done this before? Announcing at a pachinko parlor, emceeing weddings, that sort of thing?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、飲食業の前にちょっとな、知人のミニＦＭを手伝ってたことがある。学生サークルに毛が生えた程度の規模だったが、いちおう一年近くは続いたんだ」
lines.english: “Yes. Before I entered the restaurant business, I helped out with an acquaintance’s tiny low-power FM station. It was barely more than a student club, but we did keep it running for nearly a year.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、マジんこ？　えっ、うそ、マジでラジオ番組やってたんすか？」
lines.english: “Wait, seriously? For real? You actually ran a radio show?”

lines.japanese: 「大したもんじゃない。田舎町の海水浴場ローカルで、リスナーはピーク時でも百人はいなかったんじゃないか……まあ、それなりに反響はあったんだがな」
lines.english: “It was nothing impressive. We broadcast only to a small-town beach, and even at our peak I doubt we had a hundred listeners... Though we did attract our share of attention.”

lines.japanese: 「うわっ、ひとに歴史あり！」
lines.english: “Whoa. Everybody has a past!”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに軽部狩男の現在の口調は、当時の番組ＭＣ用に作られたキャラクターが、そのまま方言のように染みついてしまったものだという説がある」
lines.english: “Incidentally, one theory holds that Karuo Karube’s present manner of speech began as a persona created for that radio show and soaked into him so thoroughly that it became a dialect unto itself.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんな染みつくものなんすか……」
lines.english: “C-can a persona really soak in that deep...?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ。当時の俺たちは、そのちっぽけな番組ごっこに情熱のすべてを傾けていたのだ。だから俺も、本番でどっぷりキャラに入りこめるよう、日頃からスイッチをＯＮにして生活していたのだな」
lines.english: “Indeed. In those days, we poured every drop of our passion into that paltry little make-believe station. To make certain I could sink completely into character on the air, I kept myself switched ON in everyday life as well.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なるほど……じゃあ下ネタジョークとかセクハラトークなんかも、元は仕事の一環としてやむなく取りこんだものだったんすね」
lines.english: “I-I see... So the dirty jokes and sexual-harassment routine were originally things you reluctantly incorporated as part of the job.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それはもともと俺の趣味」
lines.english: “No. Those were always my hobbies.”

lines.japanese: 「むしろそっちがキャラだと言って！」
lines.english: “Please tell me that was the character instead!”

lines.japanese: 「ううむ、懐かしい。当時は金もなく休みもなく仲間同士で口論ばかりしていたが、ひと仕事終えたあとのビールはいまなお鮮明によみがえるほど格別な味だった」
lines.english: “Mmm. Those days take me back. We had no money, no days off, and spent all our time arguing. But the beer after a job well done tasted so good I can remember it even now.”

lines.japanese: 「いいっすね、そーゆーの。なんで辞めちゃったんすか」
lines.english: “That sounds great. Why’d you quit?”

lines.japanese: 「簡単な話だ、母体企業に切られた。俺たちより本格的にやってる若いチームが取って替わってな」
lines.english: “Simple. Our parent company dropped us. A younger team doing it on a truly professional level took our place.”

lines.japanese: マスターはソファーに腰を落とすと、タバコに火を点しました。彼にしては珍しく真面目な表情なものですから、俺もいらん茶化しは控えておとなしく聞いておりました。
lines.english: The boss sank onto the sofa and lit a cigarette. His expression was unusually serious, so I held back the needless wisecracks and listened quietly.

lines.japanese: 「いや、もちろんこっちも、俺たちなりには本格的なつもりだったんだ。熱意とパワーでは負けてなかったと今でも自信を持って言える。だが実績と経験においては圧倒的に劣っていた」
lines.english: “Naturally, we believed we were serious in our own way. Even now, I can say with confidence that we lost to no one in passion or drive. But in accomplishments and experience, we were overwhelmingly outclassed.”

lines.japanese: 「相手は十代なかばで海の向こうへ渡って、ハタチ前にはアメリカのクラブで皿を回していたような連中だ。悔しいが、俺たちは本気を出すのが遅かったんだな。もっと早くに夢と出会うべきだった」
lines.english: “These were people who crossed the ocean in their mid-teens and were spinning records in American clubs before twenty. Bitter as it was, we had waited too long to get serious. We should have found our dream sooner.”

lines.japanese: 夢。
lines.english: A dream.

lines.japanese: いま夢って言ったな、このひと。
lines.english: He’d said dream just now.

lines.japanese: へえ、マスターにもそんなもんがあったんだ。いいなあ。
lines.english: Huh. So even the boss had one of those. Must be nice.

lines.japanese: 「もっとも、俺はその後、べつの夢を見出したわけだがな」
lines.english: “Mind you, I went on to discover a different dream.”

lines.japanese: そう言って、壁の調理師免状を誇らしげに見上げる狩男さん。
lines.english: So saying, Karuo looked proudly up at his culinary license on the wall.

lines.japanese: 顎の不精髭に触れる仕草が格好いいなあ。
lines.english: The way he stroked the stubble on his chin looked pretty damn cool.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、羨ましっす。俺は未来に希望すら持てない、その日暮らしのプー太郎っすから」
lines.english: “Man, I envy you. I’m an unemployed drifter living hand to mouth, without so much as hope for the future.”

lines.japanese: 「自由は若さの特権だ、奔放に生きるのもいいじゃないか。だが、地に足を付けようと思うことがあれば、この狩男の城を選んでも良いのだぞ」
lines.english: “Freedom is the privilege of youth. There is nothing wrong with living as wildly as you please. But should you ever wish to put your feet on solid ground, you may choose this castle of mine.”

lines.japanese: 「え、それはアレキサンダーで正社員登用してくれるってことすか」
lines.english: “Wait, does that mean you’d hire me as a full-time employee at Alexander?”

lines.japanese: 「くくく。もしおまえが真剣に考えるというなら、俺はいっちょ人肌温めてやってもいい」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh. If you’re willing to give it serious thought, I might be willing to lend you a warm body.”

lines.japanese: 「ソレなんか微妙にことわざ間違ってますよ！」
lines.english: “You’ve mangled that expression in a really disturbing way!”

lines.japanese: ああでも、やっぱり適度におどけ入る方が楽だなあ、俺としては。
lines.english: Still, I was more comfortable when there was at least a little clowning around.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、真剣に考えることもありますけどね。でも、真面目に考えれば考えるほど、暗い未来が見えてきて辛いんすよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, I think seriously about it sometimes. But the more seriously I think, the bleaker my future looks. It gets depressing.”

lines.japanese: いつ消えるか知れない身ですから。
lines.english: I was, after all, a man who might disappear at any moment.

lines.japanese: 「適当でいられるうちは適当でいるのも手だ。いずれ嫌でも自分と向き合うときは来る」
lines.english: “You might as well take it easy while you still can. Sooner or later, the day will come when you have to face yourself, whether you want to or not.”

lines.japanese: 「てことは、マスターにもあったんすか、そういう不真面目な時期」
lines.english: “So you had an unserious phase like that too, Boss?”

lines.japanese: 「なに。聞きたいのか、この狩男のヤングライフ・グラフィティを」
lines.english: “What? Do you wish to hear the Chronicles of Karuo’s Wild Youth?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、いや、とくに聞きたいってほどではないすけど」
lines.english: “What? Oh, no, I wouldn’t go so far as to say I especially—”

lines.japanese: 「そうか、そんなに聞きたいか……俺の過去など笑い話としての価値すらないが、いいだろう、どうしてもと言うなら台本の執筆料代わりに話してやる」
lines.english: “I see. You wish to hear it that badly... My past is scarcely worth even a comic anecdote, but very well. If you insist, I shall tell you in lieu of payment for your script.”

lines.japanese: 「え、執筆料あるんすか。あるんなら遠慮なく現金でいただきますけど」
lines.english: “Wait, there was payment for the script? If that’s on the table, I’ll take cash without hesitation.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな、まずはどこから話したものか……」
lines.english: “Now then. Where shall I begin...?”

lines.japanese: 「賃金交渉からでいいと思いますよ」
lines.english: “I think the wage negotiations would be a fine place to start.”

lines.japanese: 「お前には話してなかったが、俺も昔はやんちゃしていた時期があってな」
lines.english: “I haven’t told you this, but I too had a wild period when I was young.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、もう始まってるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. We’ve already started.”

lines.japanese: 前に米田さんが言ってたなあ。何十人ものチームのアタマ張ってるとか、そういう、ちょっと現実とは掛けはなれた世界の話。
lines.english: Yoneda had mentioned it before. Something about him leading a crew dozens strong—the kind of story that belonged to a world far removed from ordinary life.

lines.japanese: 「俺は腕っぷしにそこそこ自信があってな。ガキの頃はサル山の大将になっていきがってたんだ」
lines.english: “I was fairly confident in my fists. As a boy, I strutted around like the king of the playground.”

lines.japanese: 「その頃はやれボスだトップだと祭りあげられ、すっかりその気になっちまってな。仲間や後輩から助けを乞われるたび、いちいちイイ気になって力を貸してやってた」
lines.english: “They hoisted me up as their boss, their leader, and I swallowed the whole thing. Whenever a friend or one of the younger boys came begging for help, I puffed myself up and lent them my strength.”

lines.japanese: 「いいじゃないすか、面倒見のいい兄貴分ってカンジっすね」
lines.english: “Doesn’t sound so bad. You were the dependable leader everyone could turn to.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ただのエエカッコしぃだ。俺は自分を頼ってくれる連中の期待に応えたくて、無茶ないざこざにも平気で首を突っこんでいった」
lines.english: “No. I was a show-off desperate to look good. I wanted to live up to the expectations of everyone who relied on me, so I went charging into fights no sane man would touch.”

lines.japanese: 「ガキのうちは力でねじ伏せりゃそれで良かった。だが外の世界に出たとき、武器がテメエひとりの力じゃ喧嘩にすらならねえことを知った。なのに仲間はいつまでも強い俺を求める」
lines.english: “While we were kids, brute force was enough to put the other side down. But once I entered the wider world, I learned that one man’s strength wasn’t enough even to put up a fight. And still my friends demanded that I stay strong.”

lines.japanese: 「俺は金やらコネやら後ろ盾やら、そんな武器を手に入れるため、気が付いたら落ちるところまで落ちていた。赤の他人を追いこんで、自分さえ慕われていればいいというやつに成りさがっていたんだ」
lines.english: “Money, connections, protection—I went looking for weapons like those, and before I knew it I had sunk as low as a man could go. I became the sort who would ruin complete strangers as long as my own followers kept admiring me.”

lines.japanese: 「他人を追いこむ……って、あの、ソレどんな仕事なんすか？」
lines.english: “Ruin complete strangers...? Um, what kind of work were you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「表向きは金融業だな」
lines.english: “On paper, finance.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マスターってその……だったんすか？」
lines.english: “Wait. Boss, were you... one of those people?”

lines.japanese: 「軽蔑したか」
lines.english: “Do you despise me?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや……あまりに遠い世界のひとびとなんで、良くも悪くもピンと来ないっすね……」
lines.english: “Ah, no... People like that live in a world so far from mine that I can’t really grasp it, for good or ill...”

lines.japanese: 「そうか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: マスターは親指で鼻の頭を弾きました。
lines.english: The boss flicked the tip of his nose with his thumb.

lines.japanese: 「俺が足を洗ったきっかけは女だった。まあ、そいつとはとっくに終わってるが、一時期同棲なんてままごともしてな。そう長くは続かなかったが、ひとりに戻るころにはもう新しい人生が始まっていた」
lines.english: “It was a woman who made me wash my hands of that life. That relationship ended ages ago, but for a while we even played house together. It didn’t last long. Still, by the time I was on my own again, a new life had already begun.”

lines.japanese: 「それがさっきのミニＦＭだったり、アレキサンダーだったりですか」
lines.english: “And that new life was the little FM station you mentioned, then Alexander?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、十代二十代は長い寄り道だったが、三十代でようやく誇れる城に辿りついた。俺はこの城の王だ。いまの俺の夢は、この城を守りつづけることだ」
lines.english: “Yes. My teens and twenties were one long detour, but in my thirties I finally reached a castle I could be proud of. I am the king of this castle. My dream now is to keep defending it.”

lines.japanese: マスターはカウンターの上に手を置いて、突きだすように胸を張りました──
lines.english: The boss planted a hand on the counter and thrust out his chest—

lines.japanese: 「だが戦いには鋭気を養うための休息も必要だ」
lines.english: “Yet even a warrior needs rest to restore his strength for battle.”

lines.japanese: ──しかしその凛々しい表情も束の間、すぐに表情筋は弛緩して、いつものだらけた表情へ戻ってしまいました。
lines.english: —but the gallant expression lasted only a moment. His face promptly went slack again, settling back into its usual lazy look.

lines.japanese: 「さあ鷲介、下で女性客のおっぱいを片っ端から透視した気になってゲヘゲヘする遊びをしようぜ」
lines.english: “Come, Shusuke. Let us go downstairs and amuse ourselves by pretending we can see through every female customer’s clothes, sniggering obscenely all the while.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、マスター。べつに真面目で締めるのは恥ずかしいことじゃないっすよ」
lines.english: “Boss, there’s nothing embarrassing about ending on a sincere note.”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううう、うるさいっ、ぼく真面目なことなんか言ってません！」
lines.english: “S-s-s-shut up! I didn’t say anything sincere!”

lines.japanese: どうやら軽部狩男にとっては、お下劣より真面目の方が不名誉みたいです。
lines.english: Apparently, Karuo Karube found sincerity far more shameful than obscenity.

lines.japanese: 「あまり堅苦しくなるなよ、鷲介。まずは楽しく生きろ、考えるのはそれからだ」
lines.english: “Don’t get so wound up, Shusuke. Have fun living first. You can think about it afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　俺っすか？　俺はそりゃあ……ええ、まあ、楽しく生きてるっすよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Me? I’m... sure. Yeah. I’m having plenty of fun.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。なら大丈夫だ。じきにお前の元にも、最高の女が股を開いてやってくるさ」
lines.english: “I see. Then you’ll be fine. Before long, the greatest woman in the world will come your way with her legs spread.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、したり顔でそんなこと言われても。あの、ぜんぜんイイこと言ってないですから」
lines.english: “You can’t make that profound just by putting on a knowing face. You haven’t said anything remotely wise.”

lines.japanese: しかしマスターは満足そうな笑みを崩さず、自らの不真面目さに勝ちほこっておいででした。
lines.english: Yet the boss’s satisfied smile never faltered. He positively basked in the triumph of his own unseriousness.

lines.japanese: 相変わらず、カッコわるい（誉め言葉）ひとだなあ。
lines.english: As always, the man was gloriously uncool—and yes, that was a compliment.

lines.japanese: 「はーあ、そろそろ休憩も終わりだ」
lines.english: “Haaah. Break’s almost over.”

lines.japanese: 俺は伸びをしながら席を立ちました。
lines.english: I rose from my seat with a stretch.

lines.japanese: そろそろフロアが混んでくる時間帯です。気合入れてがんばりましょうかね。
lines.english: It was nearly time for the floor to fill up. Best get myself fired up and back to work.

lines.japanese: 「鷲介」
lines.english: “Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「女ができたら俺にも紹介しろよ」
lines.english: “If you find yourself a woman, introduce her to me.”

lines.japanese: 冷やかすような励ますような、歳の離れた親友みたいな目。
lines.english: The look he gave me was half teasing, half encouraging—the look of a best friend despite the years between us.

lines.japanese: 会ったことないから分からないけど、もしかしたら父親ってこんなもんなのかな。
lines.english: I’d never met my father, so I couldn’t say for sure, but perhaps this was what fathers were like.

lines.japanese: や、さすがに父親ってのはマスターに失礼か。兄貴ぐらいにしとこう。
lines.english: No, calling him my father would be rude. Better settle for an older brother.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そんなときがきたら話しますよ」
lines.english: “Sure. If that day ever comes, I’ll tell you.”

lines.japanese: 「だから原稿料ちゃんとくださいね」
lines.english: “So make sure you actually pay me for that script.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、仕方ない。俺の桃色ラックから好きなＤＶＤを一本持っていけ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha. Very well. Take any DVD you like from my smut shelf.”

lines.japanese: いや、やっぱり軽部狩男は軽部狩男以外の何者でもないですね。
lines.english: No. Karuo Karube could never be mistaken for anyone but Karuo Karube.

lines.japanese: はあ……それにしても驚いたなあ。
lines.english: Still... that had been quite a surprise.

lines.japanese: ひとには一見しただけじゃ分からない部分なんて多々あるけど、マスターがときおり見せる有無を言わせない迫力の根っこはその辺にあったのか。
lines.english: Everyone had depths no first glance could reveal. Perhaps this was the root of the commanding presence the boss sometimes displayed.

lines.japanese: 一年ちょっとで軽部狩男のことを随分と知ったつもりになっていたけど、やっぱり人間って底が見えないなあ。
lines.english: After a little over a year, I’d imagined I knew Karuo Karube rather well. But you never did reach the bottom of another human being.

lines.japanese: ま、ひとの深い部分なんて、進んで首を突っこまないよう努めてきましたからね、これまでは。
lines.english: Then again, until now I’d always made a point of keeping my nose out of the deeper parts of other people’s lives.

lines.japanese: ただ、なんていうか、最近は──
lines.english: It was only that, lately—

lines.japanese: ──ひとのことを知るのって意外と面白いなあ、とか。
lines.english: —I’d begun to find that learning about other people could be unexpectedly interesting.

lines.japanese: 仕事中にそんな取り留めもないことを考えていたせいか、俺はフロア全体にしっかり気を配れていなかったようです。
lines.english: Perhaps because I was mulling over such aimless thoughts on the job, I hadn’t been paying close enough attention to the whole floor.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん！　その席のお客さま、まだお帰りじゃありません！」
lines.english: “Chitose! The guests at that table haven’t left yet!”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: だからその声が耳に突きささって初めて、自分の失態に気付きました。
lines.english: It wasn’t until her voice pierced my reverie that I realized my mistake.

lines.japanese: 「あら？」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: 慌てて振りかえると、クラッチバッグを手にした女性が、化粧室の方から戻ってくるところでした。
lines.english: I whipped around. A woman carrying a clutch bag was just returning from the restroom.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、別にいいんですけど」
lines.english: “Oh, I don’t really mind.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はテーブルの上を片付けていた俺に微笑みながら言いました。
lines.english: She smiled at me as I stood there in the middle of clearing her table.

lines.japanese: 「申しわけございません！」
lines.english: “Please accept our deepest apologies!”

lines.japanese: 感謝と謝罪を示す最敬礼、４５度。
lines.english: The deepest bow, forty-five degrees: the highest expression of gratitude and apology.

lines.japanese: うわ、さすが日和子さんだ。まるで分度器で計ったんじゃないかってくらい綺麗なお辞儀だあ。
lines.english: Whoa. Hiyoko was incredible. Her bow was so perfect you might have thought she’d measured it with a protractor.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん！」
lines.english: “Chitose!”

lines.japanese: 「も、申しわけございません！」
lines.english: “P-please accept my deepest apologies!”

lines.japanese: 慌てて日和子さんの真似するみたいに頭を下げたけど、お客さんは別段腹を立てた様子もなく、伝票だけ持ってレジの方へすたすた歩いていってしまいました。
lines.english: I hurriedly bowed, following Hiyoko’s lead. The customer showed no sign of anger, however; she merely took her check and strode off toward the register.

lines.japanese: しまったあ……完全に気が抜けていた……。
lines.english: Damn... I’d completely zoned out...

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を上げようとしましたが──日和子さんはまだ腰を折っていました──もう一度あらためて下げなおしました。
lines.english: I started to raise my head—but Hiyoko was still bent at the waist—so I bowed all over again.

lines.japanese: お客さんと担当教官に。
lines.english: To both the customer and Coach Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 「いや……すいませんでした……」
lines.english: “I’m... very sorry...”

lines.japanese: 「なにか考えごとでもしてたんですか？」
lines.english: “Were you thinking about something?”

lines.japanese: 先の女性が会計を済ませたあと、俺は他のお客さんの目に入らない隅っこで日和子さんに謝りました。
lines.english: After the woman had paid, I apologized to Hiyoko in a corner where none of the other customers could see us.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、たぶん……じゃなくて、してました。はいすいません」
lines.english: “Yes, probably... No. I was. Yes. I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いくら混雑してる時間帯だからといって、いえ、混雑してる時間帯だからこそ気を抜かないようにしてください」
lines.english: “No matter how busy we are—no, precisely because we are busy—you must not let your attention lapse.”

lines.japanese: 「どんな考え事をしてたか知りませんし、頭の中で誰に何をしようと千歳さんの自由ですが──」
lines.english: “I don’t know what you were thinking about, and what you do to whom inside your own head is entirely your affair, but—”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、あの、そんなやましい考え事をしていたわけでは」
lines.english: “No, um, it wasn’t anything indecent—”

lines.japanese: 「──だいたい前から一度言わせていただこうと思ってたんですが、千歳さんは今日みたいに勤務中呆けていることがときどきあります」
lines.english: “—I have been meaning to say this for some time. There are occasions, like today, when you drift off on the job.”

lines.japanese: 「普段はどれだけ気の抜けた生活を送っていただいてもかまいませんが、就業中だけは然るべき勤務態度で臨んでいただかないと困ります」
lines.english: “I don’t care how absentmindedly you live in your own time. But while you’re on duty, I need you to approach your work with the proper attitude.”

lines.japanese: 「すいませんでした」
lines.english: “I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: 俺はもう一度深々と頭を下げました。
lines.english: I bowed deeply once more.

lines.japanese: せっかく少しは信頼されてきた感じだったのになあ。やっぱり人間関係を上向きのまま維持するのは難しいや。
lines.english: And just when I’d begun to feel I was earning a little trust. It really was hard to keep a relationship moving in the right direction.

lines.japanese: なにが悔しいって、玉泉トレーナーの期待を裏切っちゃったことが、教え子としてはいちばん悔しいんですけどね。はあ。下げた頭も上がりません。
lines.english: What stung most, as her pupil, was that I’d disappointed Coach Tamaizumi. Sigh. I could hardly lift my bowed head.

lines.japanese: 「もし必要なら、生活態度の改善から対策を練りますが」
lines.english: “If necessary, I can draw up a plan starting with an overhaul of your daily habits.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、それはあの……き、機会があれば」
lines.english: “Ah, no, that’s... p-perhaps if the opportunity arises.”

lines.japanese: うひい、もう居たたまれなくなってきた。早くこの場から逃げだしたいや。おそるおそる頭を上げようとしましたが──
lines.english: Eeegh. I couldn’t bear this much longer. I wanted out of here. I began timidly to lift my head—

lines.japanese: ──腕を組んで仁王立ちする日和子さんが見えたので、慌てて元の位置へ戻しました。
lines.english: —and found Hiyoko planted over me, arms folded like an avenging statue, so I hurriedly dropped it again.

lines.japanese: 「……バッシングは」
lines.english: “...Bussing tables.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「バッシング作業の際に気をつけることは？」
lines.english: “What must you remember when bussing a table?”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、ああ、はい」
lines.english: “What...? Ah. Yes.”

lines.japanese: ええと、苦情とかいちゃもんじゃなくて、食器や料理を片付ける方のバッシングですよね。
lines.english: Let’s see. She meant bussing as in clearing dishes and food, not bashing as in criticism and abuse.

lines.japanese: 「ウェイティング発生中やランチタイム等の混雑時には、迅速な行動が求められる。ただし、お客様がレジや出口に到達しているかを充分に確認してから作業に入ること」
lines.english: “When guests are waiting for tables, during lunch service, and at other crowded times, prompt action is essential. However, do not begin until you have made certain the guests have reached the register or the exit.”

lines.japanese: 「正解です。流石ですね」
lines.english: “Correct. I expected no less.”

lines.japanese: ……さすが？
lines.english: ...Expected no less?

lines.japanese: え、さすがって誰……俺？
lines.english: Wait. Who exactly had she expected no less from... me?

lines.japanese: 思わず４５度の角度から体を起こすと、そこには微笑むとは言わないまでも、柔らかな表情の日和子さんのお顔がありました。
lines.english: I straightened from my forty-five-degree bow without thinking. Hiyoko was looking at me with an expression that, while not quite a smile, was unmistakably gentle.

lines.japanese: 「今回は作業心得を理解していなかったわけでもなく、『うっかりしてた』レベルのケアレスミスですね。誰にでもあることですけど、今後は気を付けてください」
lines.english: “This wasn’t a failure to understand procedure. It was a careless slip. That happens to everyone, but please take greater care from now on.”

lines.japanese: あれ？
lines.english: Huh?

lines.japanese: 「あ、ハイ！　ハイ、気を付けます！　金輪際うっかりいたしません！」
lines.english: “Ah, yes! Yes, I’ll be careful! Never again shall I lapse into carelessness!”

lines.japanese: ていうかこれって……？
lines.english: Wait, did this mean...?

lines.japanese: 「それでは仕事に戻ってください。カウンターのお客様のグラスが空いてます」
lines.english: “Now please return to work. The guest at the counter has an empty glass.”

lines.japanese: 「ひ、日和子さん！」
lines.english: “H-Hiyoko!”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 俺は用もないのに、嬉しくてつい呼んでしまいました。
lines.english: I had no reason to call her. I simply couldn’t contain my delight.

lines.japanese: だって、ねえ？　日和子さんがですよ？
lines.english: Because, come on. This was Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: だってあの、千歳鷲介が嫌い嫌い大嫌いでお馴染みの日和子さんがですよ？
lines.english: Hiyoko, famed far and wide for hating, loathing, and utterly detesting Shusuke Chitose.

lines.japanese: 「あの……なんでしょう」
lines.english: “Um... What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ああいえ、なにか用事があって声をかけたわけじゃないんですが」
lines.english: “Oh, nothing. I didn’t call because I needed anything.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳鷲介、玉泉トレーナーの教えにしたがい、これからも精進いたします！」
lines.english: “I, Shusuke Chitose, shall follow the teachings of Coach Tamaizumi and continue devoting myself to improvement!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。頑張ってください」
lines.english: “I see. Do your best.”

lines.japanese: ゼロからのスタートとはよくいったもんですね。いいじゃないですか！　ゼロ上等！　小数点最高！
lines.english: They knew what they were talking about when they called it starting from zero. And why not? Bring on zero! Decimal points forever!

lines.japanese: よっしゃ！　これ、アゲてこうアゲてこう！
lines.english: All right! Upward and onward!

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、俺もようやく日和子さんの信頼を勝ちえたようですね」
lines.english: “At last, I appear to have won your trust, Hiyoko.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。この目がそういう目に見えますか」
lines.english: “I see. Do these look like trusting eyes to you?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そりゃあもう！　あの初日に向けられた、魚の腐ったような目に比べたら！」
lines.english: “Oh, absolutely! Compared with the dead-fish eyes you turned on me my first day!”

lines.japanese: 「……ひと様にそんな目を向けた覚えはありません」
lines.english: “...I have no recollection of ever directing such eyes at another human being.”

lines.japanese: 「あの初日に見せられた、生ゴミにたかる野良犬をあしらうような態度に比べたら！」
lines.english: “Compared with the way you treated me that first day, like a stray dog nosing through the garbage!”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんの人格に問題があったんじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Perhaps the problem was your personality.”

lines.japanese: 「あの初日に放たれた、猫の手未満という言葉に比べたら！」
lines.english: “Compared with when you said I was worth less than a cat’s paw!”

lines.japanese: 「誰がそんな非人道的かつ非道徳的な言葉を口にしたんですか」
lines.english: “Who would ever utter anything so inhumane and immoral?”

lines.japanese: 「いやアナタ言いましたよ！　今のは紛れもなく事実ですよ！」
lines.english: “You did! That last one is an indisputable fact!”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え……？　私、そんなこと言いました？」
lines.english: “What...? Did I say something like that?”

lines.japanese: 「言ったじゃないですか！　ほら、そのあと俺が『肉球にも劣る存在！？』って」
lines.english: “Of course you did! Remember? Then I said, ‘I’m worth less than a cat’s paw!?’”

lines.japanese: 「ああ！」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: ぽん、と古典的な手を打つ日和子さん。
lines.english: Hiyoko clapped a fist into her palm with the timeless gesture of recollection.

lines.japanese: 「あれえ？　アナタいま何かおっしゃいませんでした？　非人道的とか？　非道徳的とか？」
lines.english: “Oh? Didn’t somebody just say something? Something about ‘inhumane’? ‘Immoral,’ perhaps?”

lines.japanese: 「♪いーっちゃった、いっちゃったー」
lines.english: “♪ She said it, she said it—”

lines.japanese: 「♪ひーよこさんがいっちゃったー」
lines.english: “♪ Hiyoko went and said it—”

lines.japanese: 嬉しさのあまり、鬼の首を獲ったようにはしゃぐ俺。銀のお盆を真ん中に、顔を出したり隠したり。脚を上げたり下ろしたり。
lines.english: Delight sent me capering as though I had just won the championship. I popped my face out from behind a silver tray, then hid it; lifted one leg, then lowered it.

lines.japanese: 「♪ひーよこさんがー……」
lines.english: “♪ Hiyoko went and—”

lines.japanese: 「ふっ」
lines.english: “Hff.”

lines.japanese: しかし俺の攻勢はぴたりと止まりました。
lines.english: My little offensive stopped dead.

lines.japanese: げ、やばっ！　英里子さんの援護もないのに、つい興奮して少し……っていうか、かなり調子に乗ってしまった！
lines.english: Oh, hell. This was bad! Without Eriko to cover me, excitement had carried me a little... No, I’d gotten spectacularly carried away!

lines.japanese: 鬼の日和子さんは肩をぷるぷると揺らしておいででした。
lines.english: Hiyoko the demon stood there with her shoulders trembling.
“H-heh heh...”

lines.japanese: 思わず俺は素に戻って後ずさりました。だって怖いんだもんこのひと。
lines.english: I dropped the act and backed away without thinking. Because she was scary, okay?

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん」
lines.english: “Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんは相変わらず面白い方ですね」
lines.english: “You truly are as entertaining as ever, Chitose.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　うそ、誉められた？　ええ、なんかよく分かんないけどきゃっほう！」
lines.english: “H-huh? Really? Was that a compliment? I don’t quite get it, but woohoo!”

lines.japanese: 「だけど、すぐにそう調子に乗るところが……！」
lines.english: “And it is precisely the way you let the slightest thing go straight to your head that...!”

lines.japanese: 「アッ！　いや、あのっ、スンマセンなんだか急に腹の調子が……あて、あてててて」
lines.english: “Ah! No, um, sorry, but my stomach’s suddenly acting up... Ow, ow ow ow...”

lines.japanese: 「というわけで、お話の途中ではありますが、しばし厠に篭らせていただきます！　それでは！」
lines.english: “And so, though we remain in the middle of our discussion, I must sequester myself in the privy for a time! Farewell!”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん！」
lines.english: “Chitose!”

lines.japanese: まだ説教の続きそうな場から避難しました。
lines.english: I fled before the lecture could continue.

lines.japanese: そりゃあ調子に乗るのは良くないことですけど、だって仕方ないじゃないですか！　好きなひとに褒められたらそりゃ誰だってテンション上がりますよ！（逆ギレ）
lines.english: Sure, getting carried away was bad, but what else was I supposed to do!? Anyone would get pumped if the person they liked complimented them! (Getting mad even though I was in the wrong.)
